subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Chronic myeloid leukaemia: molecular pathogenesis, targeted TKIs and treatment-free remission

steps.tx: **Chronic myeloid leukaemia** is a clonal myeloproliferative neoplasm defined cytogenetically by the **Philadelphia chromosome**. This reciprocal translocation between chromosomes 9 and 22, designated t(9;22)(q34.1;q11.2), fuses the ABL1 proto-oncogene to the BCR gene. The resulting BCR-ABL1 chimeric oncoprotein exhibits constitutive tyrosine kinase activity, driving autonomous granulocyte expansion, defective marrow adhesion, and impaired apoptosis.
steps.say: Chronic myeloid leukaemia is a clonal myeloproliferative neoplasm defined cytogenetically by the Philadelphia chromosome. This reciprocal chromosomal translocation creates an oncogenic fusion between ABL1 and BCR. The resulting BCR-ABL1 chimeric oncoprotein exhibits constitutive tyrosine kinase activity, driving autonomous granulocyte expansion.

steps.tx: The introduction of the first-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor **imatinib** 400 mg daily transformed the clinical landscape of chronic phase leukaemia. Long-term follow-up from the landmark **IRIS trial** established 10 year overall survival exceeding 85%, converting a historically fatal malignancy into a manageable chronic disease. The vast majority of deaths occurring in long-term imatinib-treated patients are unrelated to leukaemia progression.

steps.tx: **Second-generation TKIs** including **dasatinib**, **nilotinib**, and **bosutinib** exhibit greater biochemical potency against BCR-ABL1 kinase than **imatinib**. In frontline randomized trials, these potent agents induce faster and significantly deeper **molecular responses**. Second-generation inhibitors are indicated for frontline therapy in high-risk patients based on Sokal or ELTS prognostic scores, and provide effective second-line therapy for imatinib resistance or intolerance.
steps.say: Second-generation TKIs including dasatinib, nilotinib, and bosutinib exhibit greater biochemical potency against BCR-ABL1 kinase than imatinib. In clinical trials, these potent agents produce faster and deeper molecular responses. Second-generation inhibitors provide effective treatment for patients with imatinib resistance or intolerance.

left.title: Second-Generation TKIs
points: Higher rates of early MMR and MR4.5
Specific risks: pleural effusion, vascular events

right.title: First-Generation Imatinib
points: Standard initial therapy for two decades

steps.tx: Acquired point mutations in the kinase domain represent the principal mechanism of secondary resistance to tyrosine kinase inhibitors. The BCR-ABL1 **gatekeeper mutation** T315I substitutes isoleucine for threonine at codon 315, creating steric clash that blocks **imatinib**, **dasatinib**, **nilotinib**, and **bosutinib**. The third-generation oral inhibitor **ponatinib** was engineered to overcome this steric hindrance, serving as the essential targeted therapy for T315I-positive disease.
steps.say: Acquired point mutations in the kinase domain represent the principal mechanism of secondary resistance to tyrosine kinase inhibitors. The BCR-ABL1 gatekeeper mutation T315I creates a steric clash that blocks imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, and bosutinib. The third-generation oral inhibitor ponatinib is the essential targeted therapy for T315I-positive disease.

steps.tx: **Asciminib** is a first-in-class allosteric inhibitor that binds Specifically Targeting the ABL Myristoyl Pocket, acting as a **STAMP inhibitor**. By locking the kinase into an inactive autoinhibited conformation, asciminib avoids competitive ATP-binding pocket resistance. In the phase 3 ASCEMBL and ASC4FIRST trials, asciminib demonstrated superior major molecular response rates and improved tolerability compared to **bosutinib** and standard TKIs in chronic phase disease.
steps.say: Asciminib is a first-in-class allosteric inhibitor that binds the myristoyl pocket, acting as a STAMP inhibitor. By locking the kinase into an inactive conformation, asciminib avoids ATP pocket resistance. In the phase 3 ASCEMBL and ASC4FIRST trials, asciminib demonstrated superior molecular response rates compared to bosutinib.

left.title: Asciminib Allosteric STAMP
points: Spares ATP binding site, overcomes pocket mutations
Superior MMR in ASCEMBL and ASC4FIRST

steps.tx: Standardized quantitative PCR tracking BCR-ABL1 transcripts on the International Scale provides strict therapeutic monitoring. **European LeukemiaNet** guidelines define **molecular response milestones**: BCR-ABL1 transcripts must reach 10% or less at 3 months, 1% or less at 6 months, and 0.1% or less at 12 months, denoting major molecular response (MMR). Missing these time-dependent milestones signals treatment failure, prompting mutational analysis and regimen modification.
steps.say: Standardized quantitative PCR tracking BCR-ABL1 transcripts on the International Scale provides strict therapeutic monitoring. European LeukemiaNet guidelines define molecular response milestones: BCR-ABL1 transcripts must reach ten percent or less at 3 months, one percent or less at 6 months, and zero point one percent or less at 12 months. Missing these milestones prompts treatment modification.

steps.tx: Achieving prolonged deep molecular remission permits trial of drug cessation. **Treatment-free remission** is safe and feasible in patients maintaining **deep molecular response** of MR4 (BCR-ABL1 under 0.01%) or MR4.5 (under 0.0032%) for at least 2 consecutive years. Approximately 50% of qualifying patients maintain durable treatment-free remission without molecular relapse, while those who lose major molecular response regain remission upon restarting therapy.

steps.tx: **Blast phase CML** signifies biological transformation into acute leukaemia, defined by 20% or more blasts in the peripheral blood or bone marrow, or extramedullary blastic deposits. Immunophenotyping distinguishes **blast transformation** into myeloid phenotype in approximately 70% and lymphoid phenotype in 30% of cases. Management requires intensive combination chemotherapy with third-generation TKIs, bridged promptly to allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
